svg.title: Adding r d∗ 3d3, where r = [M + 2M2/v + v/2]Nδ−2, makes Q uniformly positive. Near zero it adds only a nonnegative form. This correction has finite-support Laurent coefficients and a common analytic bound. It preserves the physical curvature contraction because d3d2 = 0. Enlarging the upper cost therefore gives a uniformly positive full-space row with exactly the original dT 2 Qd2 at every period. This is the positive extension used in pinning.
